mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly shows how to group objects using only ONE property?

options.A: Group objects as magnetic and non‑magnetic.
options.B: Group objects as heavy and shiny.
options.C: Group objects as kitchen items and school items.
options.D: Group objects as transparent and flexible.

mcqs.answer: Group objects as magnetic and non‑magnetic.
mcqs.explanation: The correct grouping uses a single property – magnetism. Options B, C and D each combine two different properties (weight & shine, purpose, transparency & flexibility), which is not a single‑property classification. Students often mistake purpose or multiple traits for a property, leading to incorrect groupings.

mcqs.learning_point: Creating groups using more than one property
mcqs.question: Which grouping method uses more than one property to classify the objects?

options.A: Group objects that are magnetic and heavy.
options.B: Group objects that are made of metal.
options.C: Group objects that are red in colour.
options.D: Group objects that are larger than a hand.

mcqs.answer: Group objects that are magnetic and heavy.
mcqs.explanation: Option A combines two properties – magnetism and weight – to form the group, satisfying the requirement of using more than one property. Options B, C, and D each rely on a single property (material, colour, size). Understanding that multiple criteria can be applied together is essential for accurate classification.

mcqs.learning_point: Explaining why a material belongs to a group
mcqs.question: Glass is placed in the group "transparent materials". Which explanation correctly justifies this classification?

options.A: Glass lets light pass through it, so it is transparent and belongs to the transparent group.
options.B: Glass is hard, therefore it is placed in the transparent group.
options.C: Glass is used for windows, so it belongs to the transparent group.
options.D: Glass is heavy, which is why it is in the transparent group.

mcqs.answer: Glass lets light pass through it, so it is transparent and belongs to the transparent group.
mcqs.explanation: The correct reason is based on the defining property of the group – transparency, i.e., the ability to allow light to pass. Options B, C, and D refer to unrelated characteristics (hardness, usage, weight) and do not explain the material's membership in the transparent group.

mcqs.learning_point: Using classification to identify suitable materials
mcqs.question: A child needs a material for a spoon that will not rust when used with food and should conduct heat quickly to keep the food warm. Which material is the most suitable based on classification of properties?
mcqs.explanation: Stainless steel does not rust (corrosion‑resistant) and is a good conductor of heat, matching both required properties. Iron rusts, plastic is a poor heat conductor, and wood neither conducts heat well nor is suitable for food contact in this context. Competitive‑exam questions test the ability to apply classification knowledge to real‑world choices.
